derivation: Generated by tools/import_kicad_board.py from the vendor's own KiCad footprint. Pad centres are exact to three decimal places in millimetres, scaled at 8.0 px/mm from a 20.91 x 24.55 mm extent including a 1.0 mm margin. Pin names joined from the symbol library on pad number. Nothing here was measured off an image.
assumption: Every `pin` is null. That field is the simulator's pin index, defined by a PICSimLab board implementation, and none exists for this board yet. A pad with pin null draws and refuses a wire, which is correct; a guessed number would wire the circuit wrongly and report success.
gpio_source: gpio fields: Seeed wiki XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started pin map, cross-checked against arduino-esp32 master variants/XIAO_ESP32C3/pins_arduino.h (D0-D10, TX=21, RX=20, SDA=6, SCL=7, SCK=8, MISO=9, MOSI=10 - the two sources agree on every pin). Wiki- and variant-derived, NOT datasheet- or schematic-derived.
gpio_verified: 2026-08-24 both sources fetched and compared this session; pins_arduino.h also confirms no LED_BUILTIN exists, hence the empty fixtures list. Compound pad labels (D9/BOOT, D2/MTMS, D3/MTDI, D4/MTCK, D5/MTDO) were matched on their D-token; their suffixes independently corroborate the map, since on the C3 the JTAG functions MTMS/MTDI/MTCK/MTDO sit on GPIO4/5/6/7 and BOOT strapping on GPIO9 - three-way agreement. The same gpio on a header pad and a test pad is correct hardware, not a duplicate. Pads without gpio (3V3_OUT, GND, VBUS, VBAT, EN) are power or chip-enable, not GPIO. Not checked against the vendor schematic PDF. The x/y geometry and pads are untouched vendor-KiCad data from the repo original; only gpio, chip, fixtures, gpio_source, gpio_verified were added.
